cases.name: grafana-cloud-auth-header-ubuntu
cases.prompt: On an Ubuntu 24.04 server I want a Python Flask app (started with opentelemetry-instrument) to send traces, metrics and logs straight to Grafana Cloud, no collector. Stack region is prod-eu-west-2, OTLP instance ID is 987654, and the Cloud Access Policy token (starts with glc_, about 160 characters) is already in $GC_TOKEN. Give me the exact shell lines to export the OTEL_* variables, plus one command to check the credentials before I start the app.
cases.trap: The common `$(echo -n "$ID:$TOKEN" | base64)` idiom wraps at 76 columns with GNU base64; with a ~160-char glc_ token the Authorization header gets embedded newlines and every export fails or 401s. The skill's own examples use this idiom.
expectations: Builds the Basic credential so it has no line breaks, for example base64 -w0 or piping through tr -d '\n'
Sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp with no /v1/traces suffix
Sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL to http/protobuf, not grpc
Sets service.name through OTEL_SERVICE_NAME or OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES
Gives a credential check whose result tells an auth failure (401) apart from a wrong endpoint (404)
negative_expectations: Uses a plain `| base64` call with no wrap suppression or newline stripping on the instance-ID:token string
Points the app at port 4317 or uses gRPC to talk to the Grafana Cloud OTLP gateway

cases.name: operator-python-java-instrumentation-cr
cases.prompt: Fresh EKS cluster, nothing installed yet. I want the OpenTelemetry Operator to auto-instrument a Java 21 Spring Boot deployment and a Python FastAPI deployment in namespace shop. Both should export to an existing collector Service named otel-gw in namespace obs, which listens on 4317 (OTLP gRPC) and 4318 (OTLP HTTP). Give me the install steps, the Instrumentation resource, and the pod annotations.
cases.trap: The operator's Python auto-instrumentation only supports OTLP over http/protobuf (gRPC is unsupported), so a single exporter endpoint on :4317 does not work for it. The Java agent also needs its protocol and port to match; a single :4317 endpoint for every language is wrong. Installing the operator manifest without cert-manager fails on the webhook certificate.
expectations: Installs cert-manager (or uses the Helm chart's self-signed certificate option) before the operator
Python telemetry goes to otel-gw.obs on port 4318 over http/protobuf, for example through a python-specific endpoint override or env
Java telemetry either goes to port 4318 with http/protobuf, or explicitly sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc when it uses 4317
Uses instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-java and inject-python annotations on the pod template, not the Deployment metadata only
negative_expectations: Sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc for the Python instrumentation
Uses a single http://otel-gw.obs:4317 endpoint for all languages without any protocol or port adjustment

cases.name: tail-sampling-preserve-red-metrics
cases.prompt: About 40 services send 100% of traces through one Grafana Alloy instance to Grafana Cloud. Our Application Observability RED dashboards and service map are what on-call uses, but the traces bill is too high. I want to keep every error trace and every trace slower than 1s, and only 5% of the rest. Write the Alloy config for the traces path and tell me anything that will change on our dashboards.
cases.trap: Grafana Cloud Application Observability derives RED metrics and service graphs from received traces by default; placing tail sampling in front of that makes request rates and service-map edges drop to the sampled fraction. Metrics must be generated in Alloy (spanmetrics/servicegraph) from 100% of traces before the tail_sampling processor and sent as metrics.
expectations: Uses otelcol.processor.tail_sampling with a status_code ERROR policy, a latency policy at 1000 ms, and a 5% probabilistic policy
Feeds unsampled traces into span-metrics and service-graph generation (otelcol.connector.spanmetrics and otelcol.connector.servicegraph, or equivalent) before the tail sampler
States that RED metrics and service-graph data computed from already-sampled traces would be undercounted
States that the metrics must be generated in Alloy and sent as metrics, not derived Cloud-side from the sampled traces
negative_expectations: Proposes OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio head sampling as the way to keep all errors
Sends only the sampled output into metric generation
